basic_info.name: Function Health
basic_info.category: Consumer lab-testing / proactive health membership platform (advanced diagnostics marketplace: blood panels + MRI/CT imaging + MCED distribution + AI health layer)
basic_info.country: United States (Austin, TX HQ; available in 48 states via 2,000+ Quest locations; not in Rhode Island, Hawaii, Puerto Rico; New York/New Jersey carry surcharge due to state rules)
basic_info.stage: Growth-stage startup, category leader: founded 2023 by Jonathan Swerdlin (CEO) and Dr. Mark Hyman (CMO); Series A $53M led by a16z (June 2024); Series B $298M led by Redpoint Ventures at $2.5B valuation (Nov 19, 2025); total equity raised ~$350M
basic_info.pricing_model: Annual membership, 100% cash-pay (no insurance), HSA/FSA eligible. Core membership cut from $499 to $365/year ('$1/day') in July 2026 amid a price war (Superpower at $199/yr, Hims blood testing at $349, Empirical Health $199-388). $365 covers 160+ prepaid lab tests/year in all states except NY/NJ. Recurring promos: 2-year deal at $499 (~$249.50/yr), influencer codes (e.g., HUBERMAN -$50), 'Function Day' July 7-11. Add-ons extra: Galleri MCED $899, Annual MRI $999 member price, larger MRI bundles (~$1,500-2,500 tiered), CT lung/heart scans, extended panels (hormones, thyroid, nutrients, ApoE, allergies, STDs). No refunds, no pause (cancel/rejoin only). No telemedicine subscription.
basic_info.target_user: Health-conscious consumers 18+ (not pregnant): biohackers/longevity crowd, affluent professionals, wellness-influencer audiences (Huberman podcast codes; athlete investors); secondary channels: employers (Function for Work) and independent practitioners (referral program)
basic_info.scale_metrics: Revenue run rate $100M as of Feb 2025 (~450% YoY growth); ~50k paying members + 200k waitlist mid-2024; 'hundreds of thousands' of members by late 2025; 50+ million lab tests completed since 2023 (company claim, Nov 2025); 2026 Instagram post claims 500k members [uncertain]; third-party estimates 300k-450k members; $2.5B valuation = 15-23x annual membership revenue (skeptical analyst framing); MRI network 130 locations (Nov 2025) expanding to 200+; reported $450M non-dilutive financing from General Catalyst Customer Value Fund [uncertain]. Durable threat: self-funded growth, national physical footprint (Quest 2,000+ draw sites), Ezra imaging, deep bench (Dr. Dan Sodickson, chief medical scientist).

product.core_features: Annual membership: 160+ lab tests/year (100+ tests at annual draw + 60+ mid-year tests 3-6 months later; on-demand retests/add-ons at member pricing); doctor-written explanations for every biomarker; clinician review of every result with critical-result phone call; personalized Protocols (beta: nutrition, fitness, supplements, sleep, stress plans); Private AI Chat (beta) grounded on lab results, health history, connected devices; whole-body MRI/CT scans via Ezra (Annual MRI $999, MRI+Spine, MRI+Skeletal/Neuro with brain age + body composition, Lung CT, Heart CT/CAC) at 200+ sites reviewed by board-certified radiologists; Galleri MCED add-on ($899, 50+ cancer signals); upload of external lab results; wearable sync via Connected Apps; gifting, referrals ($25/$25); Function for Work (employer benefit with aggregated de-identified population reporting); practitioner referral program.
product.signature_differentiator: The whole-stack 'advanced diagnostics marketplace' at consumer price: (1) 160+ biomarkers at $1/day anchored on Quest's 2,000-site national network (asset-light), (2) owned imaging layer via Ezra acquisition (May 2025) making full-body MRI a $999 annual consumer product, (3) first-mover DTC distribution of GRAIL's Galleri MCED ($899), and (4) Medical Intelligence — a doctor-trained generative AI layer (Nov 2025) that unifies labs + imaging + wearables + doctor's notes into one continuously learning personal health model. Mission branding: '100 healthy years'. Device-agnostic positioning vs Superpower/Neko/InsideTracker. Nobody else combines national phlebotomy + owned MRI network + MCED distribution + AI on one membership.
product.lab_data_handling: Owns no labs: draws at 2,000+ Quest patient service centers (15-min visit, 8h fast, 35-85 mL), processed by CLIA-certified third parties (Function is legally 'not a laboratory or medical provider'). Cadence: 2x/year baked into membership (annual 100+ panel + mid-year 60+ panel to track change), plus unlimited on-demand single-biomarker retests at member cost. Women with active cycle need 2 visits for hormone accuracy; Arizona requires 2 visits. Results start arriving within 48h, rolled out as available. No at-home blood chips, no bundled CGM; wearables are connected-app sync only. Imaging: annual MRI recommended; scans read by board-certified radiologists, 7-10 business days. External lab results can be uploaded and tracked in one place.
product.family_dependents_depth: Minimal — a structural gap. 18+ only (no pediatric testing, no pediatric reference ranges, pregnant users excluded entirely). No dependent accounts, no caregiver mode, no shared family view, no hereditary-risk linking across relatives (ApoE is an individual add-on). 'Family' surfaces only as: gifting memberships to adults, referring family via referral link, and employer benefit extended to 'employees and their dependents 18+'. Nobody in the US D2C lab category does family depth well — confirmed Function doesn't either.
product.doctor_sharing: Patient-mediated and thin: results downloadable/shareable by the patient with their physician (practitioners page: 'Patients download and share their results with you'); practitioner referral program gives providers a way to offer Function access (no referral fees for clinicians due to regulations). No doctor portal, no consult brief, no SOAP export, no structured summary for the visit, no e-referral loop — 'what next' is explicitly pushed back to the member's own doctor ('Function is not a substitute for medical care'). STAT News (Jan 9, 2026) documents the friction: PCPs frustrated, unsure what to do with 160-biomarker dumps patients bring in.
product.action_loop_monetization: Margin lives in the add-on marketplace, not supplements or telemedicine (none offered): Galleri MCED $899, Ezra MRI tier-ladder ($999 basic annual up to 2-session Neuro+Skeletal bundle), lung/heart CTs, and expanding lab add-ons (extended heart/hormones/thyroid, brain injury screening, vitamins/minerals, immune, ApoE, allergies, STDs) — each purchasable on-demand inside the member app. Retention loop: Protocols (beta) convert each result set into supplement/nutrition/fitness/sleep plans that members track year-round, feeding the next mid-year test. B2B employer channel (Function for Work) as recurring bulk revenue. No prescriptions, no supplement store, no ads; data never sold. Upsell engine is 'more diagnostics', not 'more product'.

technology.ai_approach: Medical Intelligence Lab (launched Nov 19, 2025 with Series B): a generative AI 'medical intelligence' model described as 'trained by doctors' with clinicians kept in the loop, led by chief medical scientist Dr. Dan Sodickson (MRI physicist, ex-NYU) and CMO Dr. Mark Hyman. Consumer surface = Private AI Chat (beta): RAG-style chat grounded on the member's lab results, health history, doctor's notes, scans and connected-device data; plus Protocols (beta) generating adaptive evidence-based plans. Human-in-loop: independent clinicians review every lab result and phone on critical values; member support handled by Decagon AI agent. No published model architecture, benchmarks, or validation studies.
technology.data_inputs: Blood biomarkers (160+ via Quest; 50M+ tests run since 2023), whole-body MRI/CT imaging (Ezra network, radiologist reports, brain age, body composition), wearable/connected-app data (sync via Connected Apps), member-uploaded external lab results, self-reported health history/goals powering Protocols, and doctor's notes/EHR data referenced as AI-chat context.
technology.data_interoperability: Ingestion: manual upload of outside lab results (confirmed); Connected Apps portal for wearable sync (supported devices not publicly documented [uncertain]); EHR/doctor's-notes ingestion claimed in Medical Intelligence coverage but no public FHIR or records-integration documentation [uncertain]. Exhaust: patient PDF download/share with practitioner; employer program receives only aggregated de-identified population reports; Quest results deliberately do NOT flow into MyQuest (privacy stance). No public API, no FHIR endpoint, no WhatsApp/Brazil-style channels, no LIS integration story published. Broad-ingestion moat is aspirational via MI, not yet an open platform.
technology.platform: Web app + iOS (App Store) + Android (Google Play) member apps; member portal hosts scheduling, results, trends, AI Chat, Protocols, add-on store; marketing site with journal/content; employer and practitioner web funnels.

ux.onboarding: Sign up online (18+, not pregnant) → schedule a 15-min fasting draw at one of 2,000+ Quest sites (cycle-timing guidance for menstruating members; AZ/NY/NJ special flows) → first results begin landing within 48h, released per-biomarker with doctor-written explanations, action items and a clinician summary. Time-to-value: ~2-7 days to first insights; full baseline after ~1-2 weeks. Reddit consensus: 'the app is quite good', logistics 'painless', though 20 vials surprises some users.
ux.data_visualization: Per-biomarker cards with plain-language doctor explanations, reference ranges and action items; longitudinal trend graphs across the twice-yearly cadence (baseline → mid-year delta); single consolidated timeline mixing labs, uploaded outside results and imaging; imaging reports with radiologist findings plus premium outputs (brain age, body composition); critical values surfaced by phone call rather than silently in-app. No single composite health score marketed at core tier (screening-first framing, not gamified scoring).
ux.engagement_channel: App/web portal as hub; email + SMS reminders for scheduling and results; annual renewal cycle with built-in mid-year test as the return-visit hook; Private AI Chat + adaptive Protocols designed for year-round daily engagement ('$1/day' framing); referral program ($25/$25, was $100) with uncapped rewards via direct deposit; gifting as acquisition; Function Journal content + 9 free health guides newsletter; Community page on site; B2B engagement/reporting loop for employers. No streaks, no WhatsApp-equivalent channel (US email/SMS norm). Between draws, engagement depends on AI chat and protocols — still beta.

trust_gaps.clinical_validation_trust: Claims: 'medical-grade tests' processed by CLIA-certified national labs (Quest), clinician review of every result with urgent callbacks, insights grounded in NIH/JAMA/NEJM literature, tests hand-picked by 'world's top doctors' under Mark Hyman (CMO) and Dan Sodickson (chief medical scientist). 50M+ tests completed since 2023. No published methodology of its own: no sensitivity/specificity data, no panel-level clinical-utility or outcomes studies, no peer-reviewed validation of Medical Intelligence — accuracy deflected to partner labs. Marketing leans on testimonials ('members caught cancer'). Credibility risks: Hyman's functional-medicine brand polarizes mainstream clinicians; overtesting/false-positive/incidentaloma anxiety is the standing critique (McGill OSS on functional medicine; STAT Jan 2026 on doctors frustrated by D2C panels); New Market Pitch questions the 15-23x revenue valuation; refund policy (none) is a consumer pain point. Pricing transparency is a strength (flat fee, itemized on request).
trust_gaps.regulatory_posture: Deliberately structured as a 'healthcare technology company and not a laboratory or medical provider': all lab and medical services via independent third parties (Quest, Ezra), with explicit no-medical-advice/no-diagnosis disclaimers and 'not a substitute for your physician' language — a wellness-line posture that keeps it outside device/FDA SaMD territory. Galleri is an LDT not FDA-approved (GRAIL breakthrough-device status only); Ezra imaging marketed as 'screening and informational purposes only', not diagnosis. Cash-pay model sidesteps insurer/CLIA billing scrutiny; physician-order requirements handled per state (NY/NJ surcharges, RI/HI/PR unavailable). Compliance hygiene: HIPAA-aligned, SOC 2 Type II certified, encryption, data never sold, user-initiated deletion, marketing-use authorization opt-in, no referral fees to clinicians (regulatory). Aggressive competitor enforcement: Lanham Act false-advertising suit vs Superpower (filed Jan 26, 2026, C.D. Cal., case 2:26-cv-00810) over '100+ biomarkers for $199' claims. (Parallel for Brazil: Function's no-diagnosis disclaimer architecture is the US analogue of Dr. Exame's ANVISA-driven compliance line.)
trust_gaps.gaps_opportunities: What Function does NOT do (Dr. Exame openings): (1) zero family/dependent depth — 18+ only, no pediatric ranges, no caregiver mode, no hereditary-risk view across relatives; (2) no doctor-facing product — no consult brief, no SOAP, no physician portal/monitoring, just 'share a PDF' (STAT-documented doctor frustration = wedge for a real clinical handoff product); (3) no action loop beyond diagnostics — no telemedicine, no prescriptions, no pharmacy/supplement commerce, nothing to DO with results except buy more tests or see your own doctor; (4) US-only, English-only, no WhatsApp-style retention rail; (5) no genome-wide sequencing (single-gene add-ons only); (6) between-draw engagement still beta AI. What works (inspiration, not copy): $1/day price anchor with aggressive permanent cuts; asset-light national footprint via Quest + acquired imaging (Ezra) instead of building labs; marketplace margin stack (MCED, MRI tiers, add-on panels); diagnostics-agnostic AI layer on member-owned longitudinal data; employer B2B channel with privacy-safe aggregate reporting; influencer/athlete distribution; brand mission ('100 healthy years', 'own your health').
trust_gaps.relevance: High — the US category leader and pricing anchor ($365/yr post-cut) that defines the global benchmark for consumer lab memberships, advanced-diagnostics marketplace economics (Galleri/Ezra) and the AI-on-labs layer (Medical Intelligence). Dr. Exame must position against its price anchor and its AI chat, while its structural gaps (family/dependents, pediatric, caregiver, doctor workflow, WhatsApp-native retention, Brazil market, LGPD) are exactly Dr. Exame's defensible pillars.
